title: How sugar turns into caramel
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Is caramel the same as browned toast?
Why does dark caramel taste bitter?

explain.say: Heat plain sugar in a pan and it melts into a clear syrup. Keep heating, and at around 160 degrees Celsius it starts to turn golden.
The heat breaks the sugar molecules apart, and the pieces join into hundreds of new compounds. This is caramelisation, a chemical change you cannot undo.
Some new compounds are brown, and others taste buttery, nutty or toasty. Around 180 degrees you have rich amber caramel.
Keep going and more bitter compounds form, until above about 200 degrees the sugar burns black. Hot caramel is far hotter than boiling water, so it must be handled with great care.

faq.q: What happens to sugar when it caramelises?
faq.a: The heat breaks sugar molecules apart, drives off water, and the fragments join into hundreds of new brown, flavourful compounds.

faq.q: Is caramelising the same as browning toast?
faq.a: No. Browning toast and seared meat is the Maillard reaction, between sugars and proteins. Caramelising happens to sugar on its own, at a higher temperature.

faq.q: Why does dark caramel taste bitter?
faq.a: The longer sugar cooks, the more bitter compounds form and the less sweetness is left. Very dark caramel is mostly bitter.
asks: Why does burnt sugar taste bitter?

faq.q: Why add water when making caramel?
faq.a: Dissolving the sugar in water first helps it heat evenly so it does not burn in spots. The water boils away before caramelising starts.

faq.q: Why is hot caramel so dangerous?
faq.a: Caramel is at 160 degrees or more, much hotter than boiling water, and it sticks to skin, so it can cause serious burns.

facts: Table sugar starts to caramelise at around 160 degrees Celsius.
Caramel contains hundreds of flavour compounds, including diacetyl, which tastes buttery.

quiz.say: What makes caramelising different from the browning of toast?
quiz.show: What makes caramelising different from the browning of toast?

options.show: They are exactly the same reaction
options.say: They are exactly the same reaction

options.say: Caramelising uses sugar alone; toast browning needs proteins too

quiz.why: Caramelisation is sugar breaking down by itself; toast browns by the Maillard reaction between sugars and proteins.

wrong.0: Caramelising needs strong heat, around 160 degrees or more.
wrong.1: They are different reactions, though both make brown colours and toasty flavours.
